scene.note: Timetable.java runs the same lines again and again: once a minute, once an hour, once a year, once a letter.

steps.note: The countdown starts from the minutes left before the boat goes.
Each time round it says the minutes left, and something has to bring departure one minute closer.
When no minutes are left, the gate says boarding has closed, once.
The day has a first hour and a last hour, and a boat leaves every hour between them.
A counter walks the hours from the first to the last, both included.
The board gets one line for each departure.
Departures in the morning rush carry more people than the quiet ones.
A total starts at nothing, and each departure adds its passengers to it.
After the last departure, the total is the day's passengers.
The fare today and the fare the council has in mind.
Each year the fare grows by a twentieth of that year's fare, in whole pence, and one more year is counted.

value.label: years
values: years until the fare gets there

steps.note: The counting stops in the year the fare reaches the target.
A ticket starts with the boat's name, and a space ends it.
The loop looks at one letter at a time, and stops at the first space it meets.
The printer learns where the name ends, even for a ticket with no space.
